$comment: Hand-written. Each file is a content pack the importer MUST refuse, and the reason it must refuse it.
how_to_use: Feed each file to `cwbhacker import`. The importer must exit non-zero and say something that identifies the rule. Every one of these parses as valid TOML — a fixture that was merely malformed would test the TOML parser and nothing else. Verified with Python's tomllib.

packs.rule: SPEC §12: node is 1-based and contiguous; a gap is an error
packs.why: The map draws a path through the nodes. A gap leaves the overworld with a road to nowhere.

packs.rule: SPEC §12: the id must agree with the file's land and category, and with node
packs.why: A misfiled quest imports into the wrong map and is unreachable from the one it was written for.
packs.detect: id is go.advanced.07.wrong in a rust/basic pack at node 1

packs.rule: SPEC §12: at least one case must be visible
packs.why: A player with no visible case is guessing blind about the output format, which teaches nothing.
packs.detect: the only case has visible = false

packs.rule: no `expect` may be empty after `match` normalisation
packs.why: An empty expectation is satisfied by an empty `fn main() {}` — which is the starter. The node clears itself on the first submit.
packs.note: Not in SPEC §12's text; added by PM's verifier and kept because it is the sharpest of the lot.

packs.rule: SPEC §9.5: the starter must NOT be accepted
SPEC §9.4: the reference solution must pass every case
packs.why: A quest whose own answer fails is a broken quest, and running it is the only way to find out.
packs.detect: the solution prints "the wrong thing" and the case expects "a"

packs.rule: SPEC §12 (amended): hacker ⇔ quest-level time_limit_s ⇔ at least one hidden case
packs.why: The countdown is the hacker category's whole identity, and a HackerRank-style quest with every case visible is a quest with the answer printed beside it.
packs.detect: category is hacker; no time_limit_s; no hidden case

packs.rule: the same rule, the other direction
packs.why: A countdown on a grammar drill is a content mistake, not a feature — and the enforcement has to run both ways or half of it never fires.
packs.detect: category is basic and time_limit_s is 300

packs.rule: SPEC §12 (amended): code fields use TOML literal strings ('''), never """
packs.why: A """ string processes backslash escapes, so a `\n` written inside quest source becomes a real newline before rustc ever sees it — silently, with nothing looking wrong. This fixture's starter is a quest ABOUT printing a literal backslash-n, so the corruption destroys the lesson.
packs.detect: the `starter` field is """-quoted; after parsing, the two characters written as backslash-n inside the comment are one newline
packs.verified: python3 -c "import tomllib; print(repr(tomllib.loads(open('basic-escapes.toml','rb').read().decode())['quest'][0]['starter']))" shows the escape already eaten
packs.note: A TOML parser cannot report which quote style a string used, so an importer must check the raw bytes — scan the source for a quest-level `starter =` or `solution =` followed by """, not the parsed value. Flagged to BE in docs/decisions.md.

also_worth_refusing_but_not_fixtured_her.duplicate-id: two quests with the same id in one pack — caught by the UNIQUE constraint in SPEC §2.1 rather than by the importer, so the test belongs to BE's store tests
also_worth_refusing_but_not_fixtured_her.requires-cycle: a requires chain that loops. Worth a fixture once the importer exists and it is clear whether it is refused or simply leaves every node locked
also_worth_refusing_but_not_fixtured_her.map-out-of-range: map.x or map.y outside 0..1. Cheap to add; left out because nothing in SPEC §12 says it is an error rather than a clamp — raised in docs/decisions.md
